structured_output.computation:
1) SNAP household: head (68) and spouse (39, blind/disabled) are spouses living together, so they form one 2-person household. Both members are elderly or disabled.
2) Gross countable income: SSDI $30,160 + interest $275 = $30,435/yr = $2,536.25/mo of unearned income. There are no earned income, rent or utility costs, and none may be inferred.
3) Categorical eligibility: CT runs broad-based categorical eligibility (BBCE) for all households through the TANF/MOE-funded 'Help for People in Need' brochure, with a 200% FPL gross income limit and no asset limit (FNS BBCE States Chart, June 2026; CT DSS lists $3,607/mo for size 2 from Oct 1, 2026). The FY2026 200% FPL limit for 2 is 2 × $21,150 / 12 ≈ $3,525/mo. $2,536 is below that, so the household is categorically eligible.
   - Resource limits do not apply (7 CFR 273.8(a)), so the $48,000 bank balance does not disqualify.
   - Gross and net income standards do not apply (7 CFR 273.9(a); CT UPM P-5520.35: 'do not subject the unit to any income tests').
4) Net income (7 CFR 273.10(e)(1)): $2,536.25 − FY2026 standard deduction $209 (sizes 1–3, 48 states/DC) − excess medical deduction (7 CFR 273.9(d)(3)). Medical: $500 + $100 + $50 = $650/yr = $54.17/mo; minus $35 = $19.17. Net ≈ $2,308.08/mo. With no shelter costs there is no shelter deduction.
5) Allotment formula (7 CFR 273.10(e)(2)(ii)(A)): $546 (FY2026 maximum for 2) − 0.3 × $2,308 ($692) = negative, so $0 by formula.
6) Minimum benefit (7 CFR 273.10(e)(2)(ii)(C)): 'all eligible one-person and two-person households shall receive minimum monthly allotments equal to the minimum benefit' = 8% of the 1-person maximum ($298 × 0.08 = $23.84 → $24; FNS FY2026 COLA: minimum benefit $24). The zero-benefit denial/suspension rule in 273.10(e)(2)(iii) covers only households of three or more. So the benefit is $24/mo.
7) Annual: $24 × 12 = $288.
- FY2027 values (Oct–Dec 2026) were published in August 2026, after the 2026-07-03 freeze. Only the FY2026 COLA (memo dated Aug 13, 2025) existed before the freeze.
- Even under FY2027, CT DSS shows a 1-person maximum of $306; 8% = $24.48, which rounds to $24, so the annual figure is unchanged.
- The consensus $0 rests on applying an asset test or net income test that BBCE waives, or on ignoring the minimum benefit for 1–2 person households.

structured_output.definition_reading: I read 'snap' as the annual SNAP allotment for the one SNAP household formed by the two spouses (head 68 on SSDI; spouse 39, blind and disabled), summed over the 12 months of 2026 and assuming take-up. The household is BBCE categorically eligible in CT (gross income under 200% FPL), so neither the asset test nor the net income test applies. Its formula benefit is $0, but as an eligible 2-person household it gets the $24/month minimum: $288/yr.
structured_output.ambiguity: A 2016 CT Office of Legislative Research report and some third-party sites describe CT categorical eligibility as also requiring net income at or below 100% FPL; I saw that report's wording only in search snippets because the legislature site failed a certificate check. If CT's BBCE really imposed such a net test, the household (net ≈ $2,308 vs. FY2026 net limit ≈ $1,763) would fall back to regular rules. The elderly/disabled asset limit ($4,500) would then disqualify it on its $48,000 of savings, giving $0. CT's own UPM P-5520.35 ('do not subject the unit to any income tests') and the FNS BBCE chart (all households, 200% gross, no asset limit, no net test) contradict that reading, so I treat $288 as the answer the law supports.
